sentences.text: ORAL ORDER
Pursuant to a private complaint filed by respondent no.2 a police report is filed against the petitioners herein for the offences under Sections 447, 448, 420, 468 read with Section 34 of IPC.

It has resulted in C.C.No.2029/2018 pending on the file of Additional Civil Judge and JMFC,
Nelamangala, Bengaluru Rural District.
Aggrieved by the same, the present petition is filed.

2. The case of the petitioners is that, there was a civil dispute between petitioners and respondent no.2 in respect of Sy.No.1/7 of Narayanappanapalya village, it resulted in petitioner no.1 preferring O.S.No.1579/2009 on the file of Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and JMFC, Nelamangala, Bengaluru Rural District, which is still pending.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 also filed NC: 2025:KHC:44913 HC-KAR O.S.No.380/2009 for permanent injunction in respect of the same property, which has been dismissed after a full- fledged trial.
The petitioners have produced a copy of the judgment passed in O.S.No.380/2009 in this regard.
It is submitted by the petitioners that with a view of obtaining undue advantage, respondent no.2 has given a criminal colour to the civil dispute between the petitioners and himself.
On the said ground, it is prayed that proceedings in C.C.No.2029/2018 be quashed.
It is also submitted that subsequently respondent no.2 has died.
3. Learned High Court Government Pleader upon instructions, submits that the petitioners and respondent no.2 had a civil dispute in respect of Sy.No.1/7 of Narayanappanapalya village.

He also submits that respondent no.2 lodged a complaint with the police, but the same was not registered as the police were of the opinion that it is a civil dispute between the petitioners and respondent no.2.

It is further submitted that, thereafter respondent no.2 filed a private complaint before NC:
2025:KHC:44913 HC-KAR the Court which resulted in reference of the said matter to police for investigation and thereafter an FIR was registered, investigation was done and a police report has been filed.

However, he admits that subsequent to filing of the police report, civil Court in O.S.No.380/2009 has dismissed the claim of respondent no.2.
4.

Perusal of the records reveal that the allegations made by respondent no.2 against the petitioners pertain to trespass and forgery of documents in respect of the property situated in Sy.No.1/7 of Narayanappanapalya village.
Respondent no.2 had filed O.S.No.380/2009, which is a suit for permanent injunction against some of the petitioners herein.

The trial Court in the said case had framed the following issues:
Smt Thopamma vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146397818/
3 "ISSUE No.1

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the plaintiff proves that he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as the absolute owner thereof?

NC: 2025:KHC:44913 HC-KAR ISSUE No.2:
Whether the Plaintiff proves that the interference made by defendants over the suit schedule property?

ISSUE No.3:
Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction?

ISSUE No.4:
What order or decree?"

and had answered them as follows:
 "ISSUE No.1: In the Negative  ISSUE No.2: In the negative  ISSUE No.3: In the negative  ISSUE No.4: As per the final order"
The said suit has been dismissed.
5. Perusal of the record indicates that a civil dispute between petitioners and respondent No.2 has been given a criminal colour and further respondent no.2 and his legal heirs have failed to establish their rights over the property concerned and the fact that petitioners have NC: 2025:KHC:44913 HC-KAR illegally encroached upon the property in O.S.No.380/2009.
Under the said circumstances, the criminal petition will have to be allowed.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The proceedings against the petitioners herein in C.C.No.2029/2018 pending on the file of Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Nelamangala, Bengaluru Rural District stands quashed.
ii) The petition is accordingly allowed.
